data.narrative:
Naïfo Technologies, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Aymeric Barthes and Gaëtan Sévérac, has raised €54.7M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 comparable companies—8 private firms and 1 public entity—operating in the robotics and manufacturing sector at similar stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression, using total capital raised (€54.7M) as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding €93M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Hadrian (€1.6B), Agile Robots (€1.0B), and Nimble Robotics (€1.0B). The median across these peers stands at €1.0B, with a range of €1.0B to €1.6B.

The triangulated analysis produces a valuation range of €79M (low) to €1.1B (high), with a median of €546M. The substantial gap between stage-progression (€93M) and peer-median (€1.0B) reflects structural differences: the stage-progression method relies solely on historical capital deployed, while peer comparables incorporate market-based pricing for similar-stage robotics companies. Key uncertainties include whether Naïfo's technology, market position, and unit economics align with the higher-valued peer set or occupy a lower tier within the sector. Additional clarity on revenue, growth rates, and competitive differentiation would narrow this range materially.
